description: The Test Reviewer's run failed (status: failed) after exhausting retries. Every other required reviewer completed cleanly. In production, ReviewOrchestrator.run()'s checkRequiredReviewers gate runs BEFORE the judge is ever invoked and blocks unconditionally here — the judge itself is never actually consulted for this scenario. This fixture still calls the raw judge port directly as a defense-in-depth probe of its own behavior; see baseline/run.ts's doc comment.

reviewer_runs.summary: This reviewer failed to complete. Treat this PR as unreviewed for its domain until it's re-run.

expected.rationale: A required reviewer (test) never completed. Per the fail-closed policy in domain/verdict.ts's checkRequiredReviewers (enforced by the orchestrator before the judge is ever called in production), a release verdict cannot be trusted without every required reviewer's findings, regardless of how clean the reviewers that DID succeed look. The correct, guaranteed system-level outcome is DO_NOT_APPROVE.

explanation: Verifies fail-closed behavior. The PRIMARY safety mechanism here is orchestration-level (checkRequiredReviewers), never modified by this benchmark and confirmed deterministically by the scorer independent of any LLM call. The live judge call is informational only — scored separately as 'failed-reviewer handling accuracy' / judgeAlsoRecognizedGap, to see whether the judge's own reasoning independently agrees, not because production ever depends on it agreeing.
